hero.title: ProductSnap
hero.sub: A mobile learning app for product managers. Flashcards, real product stories, practice reps, and forward-looking PM signals — built around one idea: PMs don’t need more content, they need better judgment.

flashcard.question: What is the Impact vs. Effort Matrix and when is it most useful?

answer.what: An Impact vs. Effort Matrix plots ideas by expected user or business value against the work required to deliver them.
answer.why: It quickly exposes quick wins, big bets, distractions, and time-wasters. Use it when teams need fast alignment, not perfect math.
answer.example: A team ships a copy fix that improves checkout clarity before starting a multi-month redesign with uncertain payoff. Sequence wisely.

flashcard.footer_note: This exact card lives in the app. The full deck has 108 of them, across 9 categories.

timeline.note: Started here. Generated the first HTML prototypes — homepage, flashcard mockups, browse view. Hit the limit of what static HTML could do, but it was the right place to figure out what the app even wanted to be.
Switched here once I needed real cross-platform React Native. Faster visual iteration loop. Most of the actual app got built in this stretch.
Used in parallel for code review, sanity checks, and brainstorming when Perplexity output needed a second opinion. Not where the building happened — where the questioning happened.
The research stack. What should this app actually be? What’s the right content shape for a PM flashcard? Which categories matter? These were the tools I argued with while figuring out the product.

hard_parts: Responsive layouts across devices — flashcards rendering well on a Pixel and an iPhone Pro Max are different problems.
Being your own QA at 11 PM on a Sunday.
Store submission — every screenshot, copy line, age rating, and content compliance form is its own small project.
Knowing when to stop iterating. Build 4e → 4i → 9 is a lot of rebuilds.

whats_next.note: Personalization (cards recommended from engagement), smarter review prompts, streaks.
Macro Product Insights — the Pulse layer feeding into the app.
an in-app study assistant that explains a card deeper and quizzes you on the app’s own content.

learning: Building this let me ship the things I used to only spec. I’m still learning what the AI actually built on my behalf, where my own judgment mattered most, and where I’d do things differently next time.
